title: Retire legacy quant-v1 model variants — internal announcement + Q&A (scratch)
body:
Purpose:
Short scratch for a comms draft to notify internal teams (and thinking about customer-facing wording later) that we plan to retire the old quantized model variants labeled "quant-v1" across hosted endpoints and Dedicated pools. This doc is rough notes + talking points + Q&A to align eng, CS, and product before we lock wording.

Context / why: (one-liners to lead with)
- quant-v1 variants were an early quantization profile intended to reduce token cost; they showed higher variance in output distribution for certain prompt patterns and make debugging harder because of CPU-side emulation differences.
- We've shipped quant-v2 and quant-v2-lite with better parity, deterministic outputs for regex-sensitive customers, and ~15% better throughput on T4/RTX-class hardware.
- Customers on older Dedicated stacks still have some endpoints pinned to quant-v1 models; continuing to serve these increases maintenance surface and complicates routing & rollback logic.

High-level proposed announcement (internal):
- Today: flag to internal teams that we will schedule a planned retirement of "quant-v1" model variants for hosted and Dedicated environments.
- Why now: rollout of quant-v2 parity patches completed; key regression tests green; no customer-facing incidents open related to v2 migration.
- What to expect: 30-day notice window, automated migration tool available (opt-in or we will perform assisted migration with CS), fallback policy remains to float to nearest stable variant if parity issues found.
- Impact: low for most customers, medium for a small set of customers using exact generation parity for legacy data.

Timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (announce internal) — 2025-02-18: share internal comm & open a migration support channel.
- Week 1–2 — run targeted scans, identify active endpoints using quant-v1, reach out via CS and account owners, create migration playbooks per customer.
- Day 21 — freeze new provisioning of quant-v1 variants for hosted.
- Day 30 — begin automated migration for unresponsive/non-blocking customers; target final retirement at Day 45 if no rollback requests received.

Owner + escalation:
- Primary eng lead: Jonas Becker (eng-serving-runtime) — coordinates automated migration and rollback hooks.
- CS lead: Anika Rao — customer comms & triage for parity regressions.
- SRE contact: Riley Gomez — capacity planning for migration traffic and canary checks.
- Exec notify list: VP Eng, Head of Product, Head of CS.

Talking points for all-hands (2–3 min):
- We are consolidating quantization profiles to reduce complexity and improve model parity and reliability; retiring "quant-v1" is part of this cleanup.
- This decision reduces long-term operational cost and helps us route requests to faster, more deterministic kernels.
- We will support customers through a migration window and have a safe rollback path if parity problems are found.
- Thanks to the infra + applied-ml teams for getting quant-v2 across the finish line and for the regression harness.

Draft Slack announcement (internal-eng and cs):
[short headline] retiring quant-v1 model variants — 30d notice
We’re planning to retire the legacy quant-v1 variants used on some hosted and Dedicated endpoints. Quant-v2 provides better parity and throughput. Internal folks: please check the migration tracker and reach out to #cs-quant-migrations if you own accounts with special parity needs. Migration tooling and runbook linked in the tracker.

Email subject (customer-facing draft) — tentative:
Upcoming change: migration from legacy model variants (quant-v1) — action recommended
Body (short):
We’re writing to let you know we will retire an older model variant labeled "quant-v1". If your workloads depend on exact token-level parity or deterministic outputs, please reply to this thread so we can coordinate an assisted migration. We expect minimal impact for most workloads; however, we will provide a staging window and rollback support.

Internal Q&A (prep answers):
Q: Will this change my billing?
A: No pricing changes tied to the migration itself. Some customers may see decreased per-token latency and slightly different token counts depending on model output changes; we’ll help estimate impact.

Q: What if a customer reports a regression after migration?
A: We have a defined rollback path to revert endpoints to a compatibility layer and can open an interim routing rule to a pinned node while engineering diagnoses. Escalate to Anika + Jonas immediately.

Q: Are there any security/privacy implications?
A: None — the change is purely model variant and runtime optimization. No data flow changes.

Q: Will Dedicated customers be forced to migrate?
A: We will provide assisted migration for Dedicated customers. For compliance reasons, some customers may ask to keep quant-v1 longer — we'll evaluate on a case-by-case basis but aim to limit exceptions.

Migration checklist (internal ops):
- [ ] Run query to enumerate hosted endpoints with quant-v1 tags.
- [ ] Generate per-customer delta report (token counts, average latency, sequence length distribution).
- [ ] Outreach template drafted (CS).
- [ ] Automated migration tool sanity-tested on internal testbed.
- [ ] Canary plan + monitoring dashboard for parity/regression signals.
- [ ] Rollback playbook and short SLA for emergency re-pin.

Notes to self / messy reminders (scratch):
- Build a small smoke test set of prompts that historically diverged between quant-v1 and v2 (regex-sensitive, code-gen boilerplate, punctuation-heavy).
- Add an opt-out flag for customers that we can toggle quickly during migration.
- Check Dedicated provisioning UI to ensure we don't auto-create new quant-v1 variants once we announce freeze.
- Coordinate with billing to ensure no accidental SKU changes.
- Do we need legal signoff for customer notifications? Likely not, but loop in counsel if we do any contract amendments.

Open questions (to resolve before external notify):
- Can we get metrics for how many CI tests still hit quant-v1 in our internal fleets? (Jonas to check)
- Are there long-tail customers using quant-v1 via Self-hosted deployments (private) that we need to notify differently? (Product to confirm)
- Final timeline ok with SRE capacity during migration surge? (Riley)

Next steps (this doc):
1) Sync with Jonas + Anika to confirm customer list and finalize migration tool runbook (by 2025-02-20).
2) Draft internal slack + all-hands blurb (this week).
3) Prepare external customer email and CS playbook (next week).
4) Execute scans + outreach, then migrate per timeline.

If anything obvious missing, add below then we will cut a polished internal comm that legal and comms can review before any external-facing announcement.

End scratch.
